knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 4.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly names the four quantities handled for a GLM response family and gives a Poisson example?
knowledge_checks.body: Select mean, variance, variance function, scale.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Family structure specifies mean, variance, V(mu), and scale. The link maps μ to η and is a separate object from the response variance structure.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Mean, variance, V(mu), scale. Poisson: E[Y]=Var[Y]=lambda.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Letting link choice substitute for family mean-variance structure.

choices.label: Mean, variance, variance function V(mu), and scale (dispersion). Example: Poisson with mean lambda has E[Y]=Var[Y]=lambda and V(μ)=μ with scale often 1.
Choosing the logit link finishes stating mean, variance, variance function, and scale for any family.
For every GLM response, Var[Y] equals σ² constant independent of mu; V(μ)=1 always.
Mean and variance are defined only after writing the linear predictor η; family structure is secondary.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 4.2.2
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For Poisson and Normal GLM responses, which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: State E[Y], Var[Y], V(mu); refuse link-as-structure.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Poisson has mean-variance equality; Normal has constant variance with scale σ². Link choice does not replace these family facts.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Poisson V(μ)=μ; Normal V(μ)=1, scale σ². Refuse link-as-structure.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting link choice as finishing mean-variance structure.

choices.label: Poisson: E[Y]=μ, Var[Y]=μ, V(μ)=μ (scale typically 1). Normal: E[Y]=μ, Var[Y]=σ², V(μ)=1 with scale σ². The link maps μ to η; this question requires the mean, variance, and scale structure of the response family.
Choosing the logit link finishes stating E[Y], Var[Y], V(mu), and scale for Poisson and Normal.
Poisson: E[Y]=μ, Var[Y]=σ² constant; Normal: E[Y]=μ, Var[Y]=μ because both GLM families share the same variance function.
V(mu) is always mu for every exponential-family response; Normal and Poisson therefore share Var[Y]=μ.

worked_example.title: Mean, variance, V(μ), and scale for three families
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. For each family write E(Y), Var(Y), then identify V(μ) and φ.

steps.label: Poisson(λ = 3)
steps.explanation: For Poisson, mean equals variance and the variance function is V(μ) = μ with φ = 1.

steps.label: Binomial(n = 20, p = 0.4)
steps.explanation: Binomial mean is np; variance is np(1 − p); as a GLM for the count, V(μ) = μ(1 − μ/n).

steps.label: Gamma(μ = 8, α = 2)
steps.attempt_cue: Use Var = μ²/α and V(μ) = μ².
steps.explanation: Gamma has variance function V(μ) = μ²; with shape α the scale relates as Var = μ²/α.

worked_example.final_answer: Poisson: E = Var = 3, V(μ) = μ. Binomial: E = 8, Var = 4.8. Gamma: E = 8, Var = 32, V(μ) = μ².
worked_example.common_pitfall: Using V(μ) = μ for Gamma, or forgetting the (1 − p) factor in the Binomial variance.
